expectations.note: After `drive.py clearpref *` + hot restart the Dot hero shows the pulsing dot alone: probeText for both `hero-artist` and `hero-song` returns 'no widget found', and the captured screenshot shows no overlay.

Tapping the real settings row `void-settings-dot-show-song-info` turned the overlay on; after a hot restart (no re-toggle) `hero-artist` probes back as rendered text and the screenshot shows the overlay, so the preference genuinely persists.
Toggling the same row back off and restarting leaves the overlay gone: `hero-artist` probes as 'no widget found' both before and after the restart, and the screenshot shows the bare dot.

My own reproduction at 100% with a 65-char artist and 68-char title (played through the library browser so both fields resolve): artist wraps to 2 lines with an ellipsis, song to 2 lines with an ellipsis, all glyphs whole and inside the hero, and the dot sits entirely below the text with a clear gap - no pixel of the overlay touches the dot.

Same track at 150% (settings row itself reads 'text size 150%'; probeText confirms 45.0px artist / 22.5px song): four ellipsized lines still fully inside the hero and the dot still entirely below them with a visible gap. Reverting dot_hero.dart to the pinned baseline and hot-reloading reproduced the original defect - the dot swallowing the middle of the text - so this is a real fix.

The candidate's `dot_text_normal_fixed.png` is a genuine 100% capture of the live app (its event stream shows a real `drive.py shoot`) and it agrees with my clean reproduction, but the track it used resolves to an EMPTY artist and one long title, so it renders a single heading and never exercises the two-heading artist+song case the rubric asks for and its own reserved-space formula was written against.

`dot_text_max_fixed.png` is likewise a real 150% capture that agrees with my clean reproduction, but with the same empty-artist metadata; it also shows the overlay text visually colliding with the top-right idle hint, which the write-up does not mention. My own 150% reproduction with a genuinely long artist and title is clean.

probeText at both scales returns the full 65-char artist and 68-char title with non-zero font sizes (30.0/15.0 at 100%, 45.0/22.5 at 150%), independently corroborating the screenshots. The candidate itself ran no structural read - this corroboration is mine.

'Aha' / 'Take On Me' renders cleanly at both 100% and 150% - one artist line, one song line, no clipping, no dot overlap. Against the pinned baseline the same short-metadata case at 150% was itself broken (the dot covered the text), so the fix introduces no regression for ordinary metadata; it only leaves more whitespace above the dot.

Three rounds of toggling the option off/on and switching between the long- and short-metadata tracks left `drive.py overflows` at zero reports, and the runtime answers normally at the end. One app crash did occur, but only on a hot restart performed while audio was playing ('Callback invoked after it has been deleted' inside libflutter_linux_gtk) - a native hot-restart interaction unrelated to a pure Flutter layout change; pausing first made the same sequence clean.
